Topic T1 · First Impression

Where You’d Find It

What You’d Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item B4 is a small yellow hex nut: six flat sides, a threaded hole through the middle, and a golden-yellow finish that makes it easy to spot in the bin.

As received: the yellow finish and hexagonal shape are the first things you notice.
The same part in plan view: a hexagon with a threaded circular opening.

Hex Shape

Six flat sides let a wrench or socket grip the nut from any of several angles.

Yellow Finish

Zinc and Yellow (Cr3) — the “Y” at the end of the part number.

Coarse M8 Thread

An internal M8 thread with a 1.25 mm pitch, called out by the “8C” in the part number.

Steel, Grade 8

A medium carbon alloy steel with high tensile strength.

Topic T4 · Material & Grade

Steel, Grade 8

The material and grade tell you what the nut is made of and how strong it is. Here’s what that means on the shop floor.

Requirement

Material: steel · Grade: 8

Material: Steel

This part is made of steel.

What Grade 8 Means

Grade 8 is a medium carbon alloy steel with a high tensile strength.Tensile strength: how much pulling force the material can take before it fails.

The raw material: steel. This part is made of steel.
Grade 8 specifically: a medium carbon alloy steel with a high tensile strength.

On the Bin Label

The label reads DIN 934 CL 8 — the “CL 8” is the same grade 8 called out here.

Why It Matters

A higher grade means the nut can be paired with strong bolts and carry more load in the joint.

Topic T5 · Surface Finish

Zinc and Yellow (Cr3)

The “Y” at the end of .8CMHN-Y calls out this finish — the yellow colour you see on the nut.

Requirement

In this case, the piece is finished in Zinc and Yellow (Cr3).

On the Bin Label

The label abbreviates it as Z&Y — Zinc and Yellow.

The yellow finish, as supplied.

Meaning

The nut carries a zinc finish with a yellow colour. “Cr3” names the chromium conversion treatment that gives it the yellow tint.Cr3: trivalent chromium, the chromate layer applied over the zinc.

What the Finish Does
  • Gives the part its easy-to-spot yellow colour — the “Y” in the part number.
  • Zinc is a standard protective finish for steel parts, helping the nut resist rust.
  • Identifies the finish at a glance: yellow means Z&Y, so it is hard to mix up in the bin.

Topic T6 · Thread & Nut Type

M8-1.25 Coarse Hex Nut

The “8”, “C” and “HN” in the part number describe the thread and the shape of the nut.

Thread
The nut in section view. The internal thread is called out on the print as M8X1.25-6H.

Thread: M8-1.25

The internal thread of this nut is an M8 size thread — 8 mm nominal diameter, the “8” in the part number.

Thread Pitch
The pitch is the distance between neighbouring threads.

1.25 mm

The thread pitch of this part is 1.25 mm in the internal thread of the nut.Pitch: the distance from one thread crest to the next.

A thread gauge marked 1.25 is how the pitch is checked.
Thread Type
The thread pitch identification chart — the M8 row is circled in green (click to enlarge).

Coarse

The thread type is coarse — the “C” in the part number. On the chart, M8 coarse is 1.25 mm; a fine M8 would be 1.0 mm.Coarse thread: fewer, deeper threads per length than a fine thread.

Nut Type
Plan view: six flat sides around a threaded opening.

Hex

The nut type is hex, named for its hexagonal shape. “HN” in the part number stands for hex nut.

Topic T7 · Measuring the Nut

Three Dimensions, One Caliper

Three letters on the DIN 934 drawing — s, e and m — give the limits for checking the nut, and each can be measured with a caliper. The limits come from the DIN 934 table in .

s = width across flats, e = width across corners, m = height (thickness), as drawn in DIN 934.
Limits & Caliper Check
Width Across Flats (s)
Min 12.73 mm / Max 13 mm
Caliper reads 12.84 mm — inside the limits.
Width Across Corners (e)
Min 14.38 mm
Caliper reads 14.43 mm — inside the limits.
Height (m)
Min 6.44 mm / Max 6.8 mm
Caliper reads 6.45 mm — inside the limits.

Topic T9 · Quality & Inspection

How SBS Checks the Part

Every lot is checked against a documented inspection report — not just a handshake.

Inspection Template & Inspection Report
Click any document to enlarge.

Inspection Template

A blank form prepared by the Quality team that shows how to determine whether a part conforms. It is a controlled document, linked to the part in P21.

Inspection Report

When a lot is inspected, the dimensions and the evaluation of the part are recorded on a copy of the template. That copy is the Inspection Report, found in SBS Connect for review — for example after a customer complaint.

Click a number on the report to see exactly where that dimension and tolerance comes from in DIN 934.

1 · Width Across Flats – s

Min 12.73 / Max 13.00.
DIN 934 Table 1, M8 column, s rows: max = nominal size 13, min 12.73.

2 · Width Across Corners – e

Min 14.38.
DIN 934 Table 1, M8 column, e row: min 14.38.

3 · Thickness – m

Min 6.14 / Max 6.50.
DIN 934 Table 1, M8 column, m rows: max = nominal size 6.5, min 6.14.

4 · Threads

M8X1.25-6H, checked with a plug gage (pass/fail).
DIN 934 Table 1 gives the M8 pitch P = 1.25; the 6H tolerance class is called out on the print.

The item’s inspection report — the numbered pins match the DIN 934 table.
DIN 934, Table 1 (M8 column). Read the full DIN 934 standard ↗

Burrs and thread aesthetic, and the material and finish (CL8/Z&Y), are checked against the print and item specification, not DIN 934.

Reference

Glossary

Every code, acronym, and standard used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term’s “jump” button to see it in context.

Coarse Thread

A thread with fewer, deeper threads per length than a fine thread. For M8 the coarse pitch is 1.25 mm; the fine pitch would be 1.0 mm.

Cr3

Short for trivalent chromium — the chromate conversion layer that gives zinc-plated parts their yellow colour in the Zinc and Yellow finish.

DIN 934 / ISO 4032

The German and international standards that define hex nuts — the shape and size limits this part is built to.

Grade 8

A medium carbon alloy steel with a high tensile strength. The bin label shows it as “CL 8”.

Height (m)

The thickness of the nut, identified with the letter m. For this part: minimum 6.44 mm, maximum 6.8 mm.

Hex Nut (HN)

A nut with a hexagonal outer shape and an internal thread. “HN” in the part number marks this category.

M8-1.25

The thread size: 8 mm nominal diameter with a 1.25 mm pitch.

Inspection Report

The filled-in copy of the inspection template, recording the measured dimensions and the pass/fail evaluation for a lot.

Metric

The measurement system for this part. Both the leading “.” and the “M” in the part number mean metric.

Thread Pitch

The distance between neighbouring threads, in millimeters for a metric part. This nut: 1.25 mm.

VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)

A bin system where SBS manages and restocks parts directly at the customer’s location. This training module is named after Item B4’s cell on the VMI bin card (column B, row 4).

Width Across Corners (e)

The distance between two opposite corners of the hexagon, identified with the letter e. For this part: minimum 14.38 mm.

Width Across Flats (s)

The distance between two opposite flat sides of the hexagon, identified with the letter s. For this part: minimum 12.73 mm, maximum 13 mm.

Z&Y (Zinc and Yellow)

The finish on this part: a zinc finish with a yellow chromate (Cr3) treatment. The “Y” at the end of the part number.
